chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Shu'ayb al-Aqraqufi who said:
I said to Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him): It may happen that we require to ask about something - so whom should we ask? He said: upon you is al-Asadi - meaning by it - Aba Basir.
ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Sadiq designate as the primary authority for asking religious questions?
ai.summary: Recorded in Rijal al-Kashshi, this narration highlights the Imam’s explicit endorsement of Abu Basir (Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Asadi) as a reliable authority for religious inquiries, reflecting the early Shia reliance on trusted companions for jurisprudential guidance. This designation underscores the institutionalization of hadith transmission and the scholarly hierarchy within the Shia community during the Imamate period.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/281] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Shuayb al-Aqraqufi who said:
I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: It may happen that we require to ask about something - so whom should we ask? He said: upon you is al-Asadi - meaning by it - Aba Basir.
